dedupe_keys.name: google project sunroof data explorer rooftop solar technical potential by area

description: Project Sunroof uses Google's mapping and computing resources to show the potential of rooftop solar power for single houses and, through its data explorer, for zip codes, cities, counties and states, estimating technical potential irrespective of financial or societal constraints. According to its methodology note, last updated in February 2017, Google processes aerial imagery into a digital surface model covering the part of the United States where more than half the population lives, estimates shading for every roof point for each sun position, including trees and buildings within 100 to 150 m, and derives usable roof space, pitch and azimuth; typical weather data then give energy production from panels on viable roof areas. Coverage: roughly 60 million buildings in portions of all 50 states and Washington, D.C., as of the methodology note. Access: free web data explorer. Licence: Google terms. Caveats: the provider site loads only with scripts and could not be read here, the methodology dates from 2017, and potential is technical, not economic. Simulation uses are area-level rooftop PV potential for distributed generation and building energy scenarios. Related records: the NREL PV Rooftop Database.
